region_label: Cool & unusual — estates, inn buyouts, compounds
notes: CATEGORY beat, not a geography. Angles that paid off, in order: (1) SMALL-INN BUYOUTS — this is the single strongest angle for this group. Several 7-10 room inns within 90 min to 2.5 hrs explicitly advertise renting the entire property, and inn rooms are disproportionately king beds. (2) MULTI-UNIT FARM/RETREAT COMPOUNDS that book as a cluster (Chinsegut Hill, Wonderfield Farm). (3) GLAMPING VILLAGES where 4-5 units = the whole group and each unit has a king bed and a real fireplace (Westgate Takoda Village is the standout here). (4) BOAT-ONLY ISLAND INNS (Cabbage Key, Useppa) — trophy-tier but logistically heavy. Angles that did NOT pay off: Plum Guide / Kip Hideaways / Boutique Homes have thin-to-no West Florida inventory (Kip is UK/Ireland only); Inspirato and Exclusive Resorts are members-only with no discoverable Tampa-area 7BR; LVH Global is Miami-side. Architecture Sarasota DOES rent Paul Rudolph landmarks (Umbrella House, Cocoon House) overnight on a case-by-case basis and one 2018 report put the Umbrella House at $6,000/night — but they are 1-3 bedroom houses, so they are a great 'one special night' add-on, not a base for 16 people; worth a call to Architecture Sarasota if the family wants a splurge dinner/afternoon. Dead ends confirmed so they aren't re-chased: Don Vicente de Ybor Historic Inn (Tampa) is CLOSED and converted to office/retail; Dreamcatcher Island (Homosassa) sold in 2023 and its rental site is offline; Little Bokeelia Island is listed for sale at $29.5M with no verifiable current nightly booking channel; The Hacienda Hotel (New Port Richey, restored 1927 landmark) is lovely but 40 rooms — too big to buy out. FETCH NOTES: Airbnb and Vrbo listing pages could not be fetched directly (expected); Tripadvisor, Expedia and herlong.com root returned 403/429; Hipcamp and Glamping Hub are JS-rendered and returned 'Loading...'. Where that happened I pulled facts from search snippets and from the properties' own sites and marked availability honestly. NO live Dec 19-27 2026 availability was verifiable anywhere — every entry is 'unknown'. For inns, the load-bearing fact is whether they do buyouts at all and who to call; those phone numbers are in the records. CALL ORDER I'd suggest: Sea Breeze Manor (727-343-4445), Heron Cay (352-383-4050), Herlong Mansion (352-466-3322), Westgate group sales (855-591-8124), Cabbage Key (239-283-2278).

properties.name: Sea Breeze Manor Inn
properties.source: Sea Breeze Manor Inn (direct, independent inn)
properties.neighborhood: Shore Blvd S, Boca Ciega Bay waterfront
properties.compound_note: Seven-suite waterfront 'Old Florida' manor house plus two pet-friendly cottages. The inn's own site states guests can 'reserve the entire property' for private celebrations — a full buyout is an advertised product, not a favor. Call Marie at (727) 343-4445 / Marie@seabreezemanorinn.com for a holiday-week buyout quote. Sleeps figure is an estimate from 7 suites + 2 cottages at 2 per unit.
properties.beds_note: Site markets 'spacious king suites' and names the Barbados Room as a king suite with a private deck; a room-by-room bed list is not published. Ask for the per-suite config when you call — inns like this are usually king-heavy, which matches the group's preference.
properties.price_note: No rates published on the inn's own site and no buyout price stated anywhere I could verify. Quoted by the innkeeper. Booking engine is at secure.thinkreservations.com/seabreezemanorinn/reservations if you want per-room pricing for Dec 19-27.
amenities: across from Boca Ciega Bay beach
properties.why: The single best fit on this list for the brief: seven waterfront king suites that book as one property, 35 minutes from TPA, with breakfast cooked for you every morning of Christmas week and Gulfport's art-district main street two blocks away. Nobody has to cook, nobody has to drive, and everyone gets a real bed.
properties.cons: It is an inn, not a house — the 'living room' is a shared parlor and there is no big private family kitchen for a Christmas dinner you cook yourselves. No pool. Buyout over the holidays may be refused or carry a premium; unverified.
properties.availability_note: Could not check Dec 19-27 2026. The inn publishes no calendar on its marketing site; live inventory sits behind its ThinkReservations booking engine.
properties.min_stay_note: Not stated. Ask about a holiday-week minimum and the buyout minimum together.

properties.name: Heron Cay Lakeview Bed & Breakfast
properties.neighborhood: 495 W Old US Hwy 441, overlooking Lake Dora
properties.compound_note: Eight-suite Victorian-style inn on three landscaped acres above Lake Dora. Eight rentable rooms is exactly the group's target if you take the whole house. Buyout is not advertised on the site — call Margie direct at 352-383-4050 / Innkeeper@heroncay.com. Sleeps 16 assumes 2 per suite.
properties.beds_note: Not stated. The site confirms every room has a full private bath with tub and shower, TV, mini-fridge, robes, and a 4+ course gourmet breakfast, but does not publish bed types. Room names seen: 'Queen Victoria', 'ZOI Garden' (ADA-compliant, pet friendly).
properties.price_note: ESTIMATE ONLY: 8 rooms x ~$250. Basis is OTA-listed nightly rates of roughly $205-$305 per room depending on room type. No buyout rate published or quoted.
properties.why: Six natural wood-burning fireplaces and eight suites, in the town that calls itself Florida's Christmas capital — Mount Dora's month-long light display and lakefront village are a 5-minute drive. For a multi-generational Christmas that wants to actually feel like Christmas, this is the most atmospheric option within two hours of Tampa.
properties.cons: Nearly two hours from TPA and inland, so no beach day without a long drive. No pool (an OTA listing mentions 'private in-room pools' which the inn's own site does not corroborate — verify). Bed configuration unknown, so the king-bed preference is unconfirmed.
properties.availability_note: Not checkable. No public calendar; the inn's site has no live booking widget I could query for Dec 2026.

properties.name: Herlong Mansion Bed & Breakfast Inn
properties.neighborhood: 402 NE Cholokka Blvd, historic downtown Micanopy
properties.compound_note: 1845 pine farmhouse rebuilt as a columned Greek Revival mansion, on the National Register of Historic Places. A venue listing describes '10 bedrooms and 13 bath plus 2 additional cottages on the property', and multiple guest reviews describe renting the whole mansion for a weekend with ~24 friends and family staying on site. Whole-property rental is an established thing here. Contact (352) 466-3322.
properties.beds_note: Not stated. OTA rate tiers imply a mix — 'Queen' rooms and a 'Deluxe' tier are priced separately, so at least some rooms are queens rather than kings.
properties.price_note: ESTIMATE ONLY: 10 rooms x ~$250. Basis is OTA-listed rates of $256-$286 for queen rooms and up to $579 for a deluxe room. Whole-mansion buyout is by quote — no published number.
properties.why: This is the real trophy-mansion answer: a whole Greek Revival landmark, 10 bedrooms plus two cottages, taken over by one family for the week, in a one-street antique town that looks like a movie set. Reviews confirm the whole-property rental actually happens.
properties.cons: Two hours from Tampa and firmly inland — no water, no beach, and Micanopy itself is tiny (dinner options are limited). Room count and bed types come from a third-party venue listing, not the inn's own page, which I could not load (403). Verify the count before committing.
properties.drive_note: ~2 hrs from Tampa International (TPA), just south of Gainesville
properties.availability_note: herlong.com returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching; Tripadvisor and Expedia returned 403/429. No calendar seen for Dec 2026.
properties.min_stay_note: Reviews reference weekend-length whole-property rentals; an 8-night holiday buyout is unverified.

properties.name: Cabbage Key Inn & Cottages
properties.neighborhood: Pine Island Sound, boat access only from Pineland/Bokeelia
properties.compound_note: A 100-acre private island with the historic inn (six newly remodeled rooms) plus six cottages: Dollhouse, Cabbage Patch, Tarpon, Blue Heron, Snook (two-story, 3BR/2BA) and Harborview (two-story stilt). Twelve rentable units in total, so the family can take a clean sub-buyout — e.g. all six inn rooms plus Snook and Harborview — or the entire island. No formal buyout program is advertised; call (239) 283-2278.
properties.beds_note: Not stated per room on the rates or accommodations pages. Only structural detail given: Snook Cottage is a two-story three-bedroom, two-bath air-conditioned stilt cottage; Harborview is a spacious two-story stilt cottage.
properties.price_note: Computed from the inn's own published holiday-season rates (holiday stays are billed at high-season Fri/Sat rates): six inn rooms at $235+$235+$265+$320+$320+$320 = $1,695, plus Snook $555 and Harborview $745 = $2,995/night before tax; x8 nights = $23,960. Taking the ENTIRE island (all 12 units) would run roughly $4,890/night. The site notes discounts are offered for extended stays.
amenities: private island, no cars and no paved roads
properties.why: Take over an Old Florida island for Christmas week — 1930s inn, the famous dollar-bill bar, no cars, and the only other people around are day-trippers off the lunch boat. It is the most memorable place on this list and the price for a sub-buyout is genuinely reasonable.
properties.cons: The logistics are the whole story: ~2 hr 15 min drive to Pineland or Bokeelia, then a boat, then you are dependent on the island's one restaurant for eight days with no car. Bed configs unpublished, so the king preference is a coin flip. Two-night minimum is stated but holiday minimums may be longer.
properties.drive_note: ~2 hrs 15 min from TPA to the Pine Island marinas, plus a 20-45 min boat transfer
properties.availability_note: Rates page confirms holiday pricing exists and that a two-night minimum applies to all stays, but there is no public calendar. Dec 19-27 2026 not verified.
properties.min_stay_note: Two-night minimum on all stays; holiday-period minimums not specified.

properties.name: Takoda Village Luxe Teepees, Westgate River Ranch
properties.source: Westgate River Ranch Resort & Rodeo (direct, group sales)
properties.neighborhood: 3200 River Ranch Blvd, on the Kissimmee River east of Lake Wales
properties.compound_note: Takoda Village holds 12 Luxe Teepees clustered under 100-year-old oaks with shared fire pits, a Chickee Hut, gas grills and hammocks. Each teepee sleeps 4. Book 5 for the group (20 beds) and you effectively have your own village corner; the resort publishes a group-rate program at 5+ teepees and a dedicated sales line at 10+. Group Sales: 855-591-8124.
properties.beds_note: Verified from Westgate's own pages: each Luxe Teepee has 1 king bed and 1 full sleeper sofa, sleeping up to 4. Counts above are for a 5-teepee block — every adult couple gets a king, which is the closest thing on this list to 'king beds in all bedrooms'.
properties.price_note: No nightly rate published. Group pricing is quoted by phone; a reduced group rate is advertised at 5+ teepees. Do not assume a number.
amenities: double-sided stone-hearth fireplace in every teepee
horseback riding, airboats, skeet, swamp buggy
properties.why: Every unit has a real double-sided stone fireplace and a king bed, the group is clustered together in its own oak-shaded village, and there is a genuine Saturday-night rodeo and a working dude ranch outside the door. For a multi-generational group with kids and grandparents who all want something to do, this beats a house with a pool.
properties.cons: Not a house — no shared kitchen or big private dining room for a family Christmas dinner (you eat at resort outlets or grill). Teepees sleep 4 each with only one real bed, so teens end up on sleeper sofas. Deep in the middle of the state, 1h45 from TPA and an hour from anything.
properties.drive_note: ~1 hr 45 min from Tampa International (TPA), via SR-60 east past Lake Wales
properties.availability_note: Group inventory is not exposed publicly. Christmas week at a resort this size will be in demand — call group sales early.
properties.min_stay_note: Not stated; group rates require a 5-teepee minimum.

properties.name: Chinsegut Hill Retreat & Manor House
properties.source: Chinsegut Hill Retreat and Conference Center (City of Brooksville)
properties.neighborhood: 22495 Chinsegut Hill Road, on the highest hill in the region
properties.compound_note: Seven cottages, each with four en-suite bedrooms, sharing a dining hall (65-75 seats) and conference building, on the grounds of the 1850s Chinsegut Hill Manor House. Two cottages = 8 bedrooms and 16 beds for the family; the whole site holds 56. Cottages 3-7 have both front and back porches. Reserve through the City of Brooksville Parks & Rec at 352-754-4031.
properties.beds_note: Verified from the retreat's own page: 'four bedrooms with two twin beds each', all with private bathrooms with showers. Counts above are for two cottages (8 bedrooms x 2 twins). This is the one entry that flatly fails the king-bed preference.
properties.price_note: No rates published. The site says 'the rates are the same for each cottage' but gives no figure. Quote by phone or the site's contact form.
amenities: 1850s National Register manor house on site
properties.why: The cheapest way on this list to get a whole hilltop estate to yourselves — an antebellum manor house, 1930s-era retreat grounds, a dining hall big enough to seat the entire extended family for Christmas dinner, and it is only an hour from Tampa.
properties.cons: Twin beds throughout — this is retreat-center lodging, not a boutique inn, and the cottages date from 1999-2000 rather than the 1850s. Shared kitchenette only (fridge, microwave, coffee pot), no real kitchen. Guests bring their own toiletries. Municipal booking, so holiday-week policy is an unknown.
properties.availability_note: No online calendar; reservations run through a contact form and the city's Parks & Rec office.

properties.name: Wonderfield Farm & Retreat
properties.source: Wonderfield Farm and Retreat (direct booking site)
properties.neighborhood: 10707 E Gobbler Drive, citrus grove bordering the Withlacoochee State Forest
properties.compound_note: A 66-acre regenerative farm and old Florida citrus grove backing onto ~10,000 acres of protected wilderness, with NINE separate rentable units listed on one direct booking site: Restored Florida Farmhouse (1BR/2BA, 4), Regenerative Farm Stay (3BR/1.5BA, 6), Kitschy Cottage (2BR, 4), Quaint Cottage (1BR, 5), A Suite in the Swamp (1BR, 4), and four glamping tents — Citrus (4), Dragonfly (4), Butterfly (2), Magnolia (2). Book the four houses plus a tent or two and the whole group is on one farm. Bedrooms/sleeps above count the five hard-sided units.
properties.beds_note: Not stated on the aggregated booking page; each unit's own page would need checking. Expect a farmhouse mix rather than uniform kings.
properties.price_note: Rates are not shown on the aggregate booking page — each unit prices separately through the site's per-property links. No total available.
properties.why: Exactly the 'orange grove estate' idea in real form — a working citrus grove and regenerative farm where the family can take over four separate houses plus glamping tents, with actual kitchens for Christmas dinner and 66 acres of grove and trail between the units.
properties.cons: Nine small units rather than one big house means booking is fiddly and the group is spread out; the largest single unit sleeps 6. Rates and bed configs are not published. Rural Citrus County — you will drive for groceries and restaurants.
properties.availability_note: The direct booking site lists all nine units but did not expose a Dec 2026 calendar to automated fetching; the Hipcamp mirror is JS-rendered and returned 'Loading...'.

properties.name: The Island Hotel (1859)
properties.source: Island Hotel & Restaurant, Cedar Key (direct; also listed room-by-room on Airbnb)
properties.compound_note: Ten individually decorated guest rooms above a landmark 1859 tabby-and-oak building that started life as Parson & Hale's General Store. Ten rooms is a clean whole-hotel buyout. Rooms 27 and 28 adjoin, which is useful for a family. Buyout terms are not published — call 352-543-5111 or 800-432-4640.
properties.beds_note: Verified room by room from the hotel's own rates page: Rm 29 king, Rm 34 king (claw-foot tub), Rm 36 king; Rms 23/27/32/33/35 queen; Rm 30 two queens; Rm 28 twin. Note Rms 27 and 28 have bathrooms ACROSS THE HALL, not en suite.
properties.price_note: ESTIMATE ONLY: 10 rooms x ~$140. Basis is Airbnb-listed rates of $125 and $155 per room seen in 2025 snippets. The hotel's own rates page does not print prices. Holiday minimums are referenced but not priced.
properties.why: One of the oldest buildings in Florida, ten rooms, a famous little bar downstairs, and a whole 19th-century hotel that a single family could plausibly take over for Christmas week in a town where nothing is open past nine.
properties.cons: Two of the ten rooms have hall bathrooms, only three rooms are kings, and it is a second-floor walk-up in a 167-year-old building — hard on grandparents. Cedar Key is 2 hr 15 min away and the Nature Coast agent is covering this town by region, so cross-check before double-listing.
properties.availability_note: Rates page states minimum stays are mandatory for holiday periods but shows no calendar. Individual rooms are also sold on Airbnb, which blocks automated fetching.
properties.min_stay_note: 'Minimum stays mandatory for holiday periods' per the hotel's own policy line; length not specified.

properties.name: Collier Inn & Cottages, Useppa Island
properties.neighborhood: Pine Island Sound; ferry from Bocilla Marina, 8115 Main St, Bokeelia
properties.compound_note: The Collier Inn has seven guest rooms on its second and third floors, from 'Whoopie Corner' up to the Barron Collier Suite — seven rooms is precisely inn-buyout size. Useppa also rents twin-family cottages and single-family homes with full kitchens, so you can mix inn rooms and a cottage. Non-members CAN stay overnight at the Inn or cottages, but unaccompanied non-member groups may need a member sponsor. Guest Services: 239.283.1061.
properties.beds_note: Not stated. Room detail lives behind /comestay/collier-inn-room/ which did not expose bed types to fetching.
properties.price_note: No rates published anywhere public — this is a private club and pricing comes from Guest Services.
properties.why: A genuinely rarefied one: a 100-acre private island club with a seven-room historic inn, a croquet lawn and pink shell paths, 15 minutes by boat from Bokeelia. If the family wants a place that feels like a 1920s club novel, this is it.
properties.cons: The sponsorship question is the deal-breaker risk — unaccompanied non-member groups may require a member to sponsor the booking, and a whole-inn holiday buyout by outsiders may simply not be offered. No rates public. 2h15 drive plus a boat, and no car once you're there.
properties.drive_note: ~2 hrs 15 min from TPA to Bokeelia, plus a ~15 min boat crossing
properties.availability_note: Club-managed inventory with no public calendar. Site confirms only that they 'remain open year-round'.

properties.name: Private Island House, Jewfish Key
properties.source: Owner-direct (Steve Ellis); also listed on Vrbo and Airbnb
properties.neighborhood: Jewfish Key, inside Longboat Pass — boat access only
properties.beds_note: Verified from the owner's site: Master #1 queen (2); Master #2 queen + 3 singles (5); Master #3 queen + 1 single (3); guest room 2 twins (2). No kings — this one misses the king-bed preference entirely.
properties.price_note: Owner site states 'starting at $1,500/night'. Christmas week will almost certainly price above the starting rate; 8 x $1,500 = $12,000 is a floor, not a quote.
amenities: 300 ft of private beach on 2 acres
properties.why: Your own two-acre island with 300 feet of private beach and a 200-foot zipline, sitting between Anna Maria Island and Longboat Key — a boat ride from Cortez but a world away, and the only 'private island' near Tampa that is unambiguously bookable right now.
properties.cons: Only 4 bedrooms against a 6-8 bedroom brief, no kings, and five of the twelve beds are singles — this works for 12, not 18. Boat-only access with a large multi-generational group over eight days is real friction (groceries, mobility, weather).
properties.drive_note: ~1 hr from Tampa International (TPA) to the Cortez/Longboat boat access, plus a short crossing
properties.availability_note: Owner-direct site has no public calendar. Also on Vrbo/Airbnb, which block automated fetching. Call the owner for Dec 19-27.

properties.name: Timberline Glamping Sarasota (Oscar Scherer State Park)
properties.neighborhood: Oscar Scherer State Park, 1843 S Tamiami Trail
properties.compound_note: Four luxury safari tents on 10 acres at the edge of Oscar Scherer State Park's trail network — four tents is the entire glamping village, so this is a true whole-site buyout at a size that fits this group. Deluxe Safari Tent (320 sq ft) sleeps 6; Double Safari Tent (320 sq ft) sleeps 4. Call 941-777-3114 / sarasota@tlglamping.com to take all four.
properties.beds_note: Per type, from Timberline's marketing: Deluxe Safari Tent = 1 king + 2 sets of bunk beds; Double Safari Tent = 2 queens. The exact mix of the four tents on this site is not published — ask when booking.
properties.price_note: ESTIMATE: 4 tents x ~$200. Basis is Timberline's stated 'nightly rates start at $152'; holiday pricing is not published. Treat as a rough floor.
amenities: A/C and heat in every tent
fire pit and charcoal grill per site
state park trails, kayaking and beach 10 min away
properties.why: Buying out all four tents gives the family a private glamping village inside a state park, 10 minutes from Nokomis and Casey Key beaches and 20 from Sarasota — outdoor Christmas with fire pits, at a fraction of what an equivalent estate costs.
properties.cons: Tents, not bedrooms: no shared indoor gathering room, no kitchen, and bathrooms are per-tent but minimal. December nights on the Gulf can drop to the 40s (heaters are provided). Only 4 units, so a group of 18 is tight. No fireplace, no Christmas-morning living room.
properties.availability_note: Booking runs through a JS-rendered engine that returned no content to automated fetching. Only four tents exist, so holiday week will go early.

properties.name: Timberline Glamping Tampa (Hillsborough River State Park)
properties.compound_note: Safari tents and bell tents inside Hillsborough River State Park, 35 minutes from downtown Tampa. Deluxe Safari Tents (320 sq ft) each hold a king plus 2 sets of bunks and sleep 6 — three of them covers 18 people. Exact on-site tent count not published; contact via the site or the Hipcamp listing.
properties.beds_note: Verified tent spec: each Deluxe Safari Tent has 1 king-sized bed and 2 sets of bunk beds. Counts above assume a 3-tent block. Bell tents are smaller and not specced publicly.
properties.price_note: No rates published for the Tampa site (the Sarasota sister site starts at $152/night). Quote by contact.
amenities: fire pit and charcoal grill per site
state park with real Florida rapids
canoe rental and swimming pool in park
properties.why: The closest genuinely unusual stay to Tampa — 35 minutes out and you are camping in one of Florida's oldest state parks, with a king bed and air conditioning. Good as a cheap, weird anchor if the family also wants city days.
properties.cons: Same tent limits as the Sarasota site: no kitchen, no shared indoor room, no fireplace, and grandparents on a state-park campsite for eight December nights is a stretch. Unit count and rates unpublished. tampa.tlglamping.com returned 404 to the fetcher — verify the site is still operating before counting on it.
properties.availability_note: Site root returned HTTP 404 to automated fetching; the Hipcamp mirror is JS-rendered and returned 'Loading...'. Confirm the location is still active.

properties.name: Outdoorsy Adventures & Resort — Airstream Village at South Tampa Farm
properties.source: Outdoorsy Adventures & Resort (also on Booking.com, Hipcamp)
properties.compound_note: A cluster of restored vintage Airstreams on South Tampa Farm — a working farm operating since 1909 and reportedly the only working farm inside the City of Tampa. Units are sold individually (named trailers, e.g. 'Amelia') across Booking.com, Hipcamp and their own site; a group would book several. Exact unit count is NOT published anywhere I could verify.
properties.beds_note: Not stated. Each Airstream is described as fully renovated with spa-inspired bathroom and luxury bedding; per-unit bed types unpublished.
properties.price_note: No rates verified. Sold per-trailer on OTAs.
amenities: working urban farm, collect eggs for breakfast
properties.why: An airstream village on a 1909 working farm ten minutes from downtown Tampa — the most genuinely odd close-in option, and the family can walk out and collect eggs on Christmas morning.
properties.cons: Weakest-verified entry here: unit count, capacity, bed types and rates are all unpublished, and Airstreams sleep 2-4 each so you would need 5-7 of them. Their own domain (visitoutdoorsy.com) did not resolve for me. Treat as a phone call, not a plan.
properties.availability_note: Not checkable. Own domain failed DNS; Hipcamp listing is JS-rendered; individual trailers appear on Booking.com with no group inventory view.

properties.name: The Amanda House — historic 1926 restored home
properties.neighborhood: Tampa Heights, ~3 min to Armature Works
properties.beds_note: From listing copy: two master en-suites (one down, one up, bed types not stated), two queen bedrooms, plus an upstairs sleeping loft with a queen trundle and a pull-out twin. Master bed sizes unconfirmed — likely not all kings.
properties.price_note: No rate captured — Vrbo/Airbnb listing pages block automated fetching. Listings show sleeps 13 (one source says 15) at 2,700 sq ft.
amenities: walk to Armature Works and the Riverwalk
properties.why: A genuinely historic 1926 house with seven bedrooms three minutes from Armature Works and downtown — the rare option where a big family can be in the middle of Tampa's food-hall-and-Riverwalk scene and still all be under one roof.
properties.cons: 2,700 sq ft split across 7 bedrooms and only 4 baths means small rooms and morning queues; sleeps 13, short of 18. Urban lot, no pool. Bed types unconfirmed and the regional Tampa agent may surface this too.
properties.availability_note: Vrbo and Airbnb block automated fetching, so Dec 19-27 2026 could not be checked. Facts above come from search snippets and OTA descriptions.

properties.name: The Grand Oaks Resort (Florida Carriage Museum)
properties.neighborhood: 3000 Marion County Rd, between Lake Weir and Ocala horse country
properties.compound_note: A 350-400 acre equestrian estate with houses and cottages for rent (each with its own kitchen, dining area and private entrance) plus the Grand Oaks Museum's collection of 160+ antique horse-drawn carriages. A group would book multiple cottages/houses. Unit count, bedroom counts and rates are NOT published — call (352) 750-5500.
properties.why: A private 350-acre carriage estate with its own museum, restaurant and stables where the family rents several cottages — the most 'country house party' option in Ocala horse country, and unlike a plain farmhouse there is genuinely something to do on the property.
properties.cons: Thinly documented: no published unit count, bedroom counts, bed types or rates, and part of the property is an RV park. 1 hr 45 min from TPA, deep inland. Needs a phone call before it can be taken seriously.
properties.availability_note: No public calendar found; resort inventory is sold by phone and on a few OTAs without group views.
